findings.detail: Closure evidence, independently verified. (1) Wording: build.yaml:41-42 reads 'dropping it, and restores the original poster when a saved configuration / narrows an owned item's badge selection to empty.'; the former parenthetical '(or removes the ArrTags image when no baseline was retained)' is deleted and the alternative attribution to the removal/uninstall drains was not used. `grep -n 'ArrTags image|baseline' build.yaml` returns no match, so no removal claim remains in the catalog text at all. (2) Correctness of the surviving claim: the retained clause is the empty-selection restore obligation of ADR-024, which the coordinator does reach; the clause makes no claim about the absent-baseline leg, so it does not contradict docs/architecture/09-persisted-artwork-rendering.md:276-282, which states that leg is unreachable through the normal generation path. No other clause, the description block, or the overview changed, and I found no new overclaim in the surrounding text. (3) Packaging: the worker re-ran `./build.sh package`; I re-ran it independently and obtained the same result, artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip with 7 entries and 619,538 bytes (attempt 1 recorded 619,561 bytes; the delta is consistent with the 63 deleted characters of prose), and `unzip -p artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip build.yaml | cmp - build.yaml` is clean, so the packaged manifest is byte-identical to the corrected source. (4) Downstream consumer: `scripts/write-manifest.cs -- --print-changelog --build-yaml build.yaml` prints the corrected sentence, so the GitHub release notes derived from this value will not carry the old claim.
